moat_against: Commodity products, no pricing power: generics and off-patent brands face structural price erosion — revenue 3-yr CAGR -4.22% and latest FY YoY -3.01% (engine)
Channel holds the power: wholesalers and PBMs squeeze generic prices; Viatris must launch new products just to hold revenue
Manufacturing quality overhang: FDA warning letter and import alert at Indore (11 products barred from the U.S.), Nashik fire/disruption expected to cut H2 2026 revenue by $100-150M
Leverage: net debt $13,088.1M = 7.1x normalized OE (engine diagnostics) on a shrinking OE base

Shrinking, churned base: biosimilars/OTC/women's-health/API divestitures cut the revenue base through 2024-25, and the Feb 2026 program cuts another ~10% of the workforce at an expected $700-850M cost
moat_for: Global scale and distribution: 1,400+ approved molecules sold in 165+ countries (Mylan generics manufacturing + Upjohn commercial footprint)
Low-cost global manufacturing footprint — the cost position a generics producer needs to survive price erosion
Legacy brand recognition (Lipitor, Viagra, Celebrex) inside a diversified base business that has produced positive conservative OE in 5 of the last 5 fiscal years

Specialty pipeline optionality: five positive Phase 3 readouts in 2025 (ophthalmology phentolamine programs, selatogrel, fast-acting meloxicam) plus a Feb 2026 restructuring targeting ~$650M of annual savings by end-2028
moat_justification: Scale without pricing power: Viatris has global generics scale and distribution (1,400+ molecules, 165+ countries, Mylan manufacturing plus Upjohn's legacy brands) and a broadening specialty pipeline, but the products themselves are commodities — off-patent brands and generics face structural price erosion, revenue fell at a 3-yr CAGR of -4.22% (engine), buyers (wholesalers/PBMs) hold the pricing power, manufacturing quality is a live liability (Indore FDA import alert, Nashik disruption), and net debt of $13,088M (7.1x normalized OE) thins the cushion. That is a weak moat: 4/10, CAP 7.2 years.
name: Viatris Inc.
one_liner: Scaled generics cash machine with a weak moat 4/10 — OE yield 8.58% on a $1.56/share normalized base is not enough at $18.22 with 7.1x net debt/OE and a falling OE trend: weighted IRR 10.18% (Tier C), IV@15% $11.28; it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$11.28.
